rationale: Bacteroides thetaiotaomicron ferments glucose anaerobically to mixed short-chain fatty acids (acetate, propionate, butyrate) and CO₂/formate. At 10 mmol glucose/gDW/h and 2 mmol NH₄/gDW/h, growth rate of 0.25 /h is supported (41 mmol C and 8 mmol N per gram biomass). Fermentation product ratios reflect typical Bacteroides metabolism. This strategy was successful in turn 0 and remains sustainable given the abundant glucose pool (24.84 mM) and ammonium (9.319 mM) remaining.
